A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JUDGE-BENCH study. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 11 LLMs across 20 datasets, including human-model agreement, response validity and prompting experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the full standard-prompt and CoT results in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The judging procedures, prompt construction, response handling and inference approach are retained. The new schema and property descriptions document the existing benchmark rather than introduce an algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The same 20 datasets, languages, annotation tasks and human/generated-text coverage remain. Informativeness is newly displayed in Figure 3 but was already evaluated within NewsRoom.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds Llama-3.1-8B to the property-level model comparison. The main 11-model comparison, nine-model CoT comparison and three-model prompt-variant comparison retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, prompting designs, evaluation metrics, decoding settings and generation budgets are retained. The corrected DICES metric label in v3 Table 4 agrees with the categorical evaluation already specified in v2; newly supplied annotation counts and property mappings document existing settings.

E4.justification: Figure 3 expands the analysis of agreement across judged properties to include informativeness and Llama-3.1-8B, and revises several property aggregates. The CoT, few-shot, paraphrase and safety analyses retain their questions and experimental setups.

E5.justification: V3 introduces systematic significance reporting for graded correlations across the standard, CoT and prompt-variant results in Tables 6, 7 and 4. Counts of significant correlations and the p < 0.05 criterion substantially extend v2's coefficient and dispersion reporting. The 1,000-sample upper-bound bootstrap is unchanged, and additional model runs are not claimed.

E6.justification: V2 Table 7 becomes v3 Table 4 with revised WMT entries: Llama-3.1-8B CoT correlations change from 0.34 to 0.18 for En-De and 0.36 to 0.13 for Zh-En, matching the retained full CoT table. Several few-shot/paraphrase entries also change. Figure 3 revises property scores, including shifting the coherence lead from Mixtral-8x22B to Llama-3.1-70B. The full standard and CoT coefficient tables otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The upper-bound reasoning and estimation procedure are retained from v2 Appendix B in v3 Appendix C. No theorem, proof or mathematical definition is added or substantively revised; the new property descriptions are explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the central contributions remain the extensible 20-dataset benchmark, evaluation of 11 LLMs, variable agreement with humans and recommendation for task-specific validation. The conclusion's added emphasis on annotator expertise repeats an existing claim.

C2.justification: V3 adds a speculative explanation that non-experts rely on surface features, questions using one judge across diverse properties, and links human/generated-text differences to self-generation bias. Its limitations now explicitly discuss shared human/LLM biases and the need to validate human raters.

D1.justification: New Appendix B specifies the JSON schema fields and points to an example and compliance instructions. Appendix D maps graded properties to datasets, while Table 2 replaces the binary annotation-availability flag with individual-annotation counts. Hardware, access dates, decoding limits, compute hours and costs remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Wei et al. (2022) on CoT and Zhu et al. (2025) on JudgeLM, briefly discussing judge finetuning against biases. A new footnote explains the naming relationship with Tan et al.'s JudgeBench. Other year and venue updates largely identify the same cited works.

P1.justification: V3 expands evaluation explanations, rewrites the limitations, adds schema and property appendices, and adds acknowledgements and author/contact details. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact, so the restructuring is limited.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with additional bars, revised colors, legend and label angles. The unchanged human/generated-text comparison moves from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 4. Table 2 changes its annotation column, result tables add significance counts, and the prompt-comparison table is relocated with a corrected metric caption.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects WMT prompt-table inconsistencies, adds significance information that helps assess weak correlations, and improves benchmark documentation through Appendices B and D. These provide a limited net gain in accuracy and transparency. However, revised Figure 3 no longer supports Section 4's retained statement that Mixtral models lead on coherence, introducing a local inconsistency that limits the improvement.
